import pandas as pd

# Define source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_46/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_46/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_46/training_2.csv"
]

# Columns of the target schema (and source schemas, which are identical)
target_columns = [
    'adm0_name', 'adm1_name', 'mkt_name', 'cm_name', 'cur_name',
    'pt_name', 'um_id', 'um_name', 'mp_month', 'mp_year', 'mp_price'
]

# Load all source tables into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    # Ensure columns are exactly as target schema and in the correct order
    df = df[target_columns]
    dfs.append(df)

# Since all source tables have the exact same schema as the target,
# we can concatenate (union) them directly
combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Optional: enforce data types as per target schema
# According to target schema:
# adm0_name, adm1_name, mkt_name, cm_name, cur_name, pt_name, um_name -> string
# um_id, mp_month, mp_year -> integer
# mp_price -> float

# Convert string columns to string type explicitly (in case of mixed types)
string_cols = ['adm0_name', 'adm1_name', 'mkt_name', 'cm_name', 'cur_name', 'pt_name', 'um_name']
for col in string_cols:
    combined_df[col] = combined_df[col].astype(str)

# Convert integer columns
int_cols = ['um_id', 'mp_month', 'mp_year']
for col in int_cols:
    combined_df[col] = pd.to_numeric(combined_df[col], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)

# Convert mp_price to float
combined_df['mp_price'] = pd.to_numeric(combined_df['mp_price'], errors='coerce').fillna(0.0).astype(float)

# Write the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_46/target_multisource_cot.csv"
combined_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
